    AI Overview
    E15 is
    a gasoline blend containing 15% ethanol and 85% gasoline, approved for use in 2001 and newer, light-duty vehicles. It is often sold as Unleaded 88, offering higher octane, lower emissions, and generally lower prices (about 10 cents less per gallon) compared to standard 10% ethanol (E10) fuel. 
    Key Details About E15 Fuel: 
    • Availability & Approval: As of May 2026, the EPA is allowing nationwide, year-round sales of E15 to reduce pump prices. It is available at over 3,000 stations, primarily in the Midwest.
    • Vehicle Compatibility: Safe for most 2001 and newer cars, light-duty trucks, and SUVs, as well as flex-fuel vehicles (FFVs).
    • Prohibited Uses: Do not use in motorcycles, boats, chainsaws, lawnmowers, or older vehicles, as it can damage their engines and fuel systems.
    • Performance: Ethanol has a lower energy density, which may cause a slight decrease in fuel efficiency (miles per gallon) compared to pure gasoline, but the higher octane can improve performance.
    • Environmental Impact: It is a cleaner-burning fuel, reducing greenhouse gas emissions by roughly 3% compared to E10. 
    For more specific information on E15, you can explore the Alternative Fuels Data Center's webpage or the Renewable Fuels Association's FAQs about E15.
